readme.content:
# 🔮 MCP + OpenResponses

**Multi-provider AI agent with real tool calling — one codebase, any LLM.**

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)
![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-MCP-blueviolet)
![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/UI-Streamlit-FF4B4B?logo=streamlit&logoColor=white)
![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Runtime-Docker-2496ED?logo=docker&logoColor=white)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green)
![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-Testing%20in%20Progress-orange)

> [!NOTE]
> **🧪 Testing in progress.** The core agent loop, MCP tool calling, and Streamlit UI are functional. Active testing is ongoing across preview models (Llama 4 Scout, Qwen3, Kimi K2) and multi-tool query chains. Expect rough edges and open an issue if something breaks.

---

## What Is This?

This project combines two open standards to create a **provider-agnostic AI agent** that executes real tools and chains them automatically:

- **[Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)** — Anthropic's open standard for defining tools once and making them discoverable by any LLM, the same way Claude Desktop, Cursor, and VS Code do it.

- **[OpenAI Responses API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses)** — The unified API spec for agentic LLM interactions (tool calling, multi-turn, structured output). Here it's served locally by the **OpenResponses Hardened Runtime** (see below), so the exact same code routes to Groq, Gemini, or any provider — you just change a model string.

The result: ask "what's the weather in Agra, its coordinates, and the time there?" and the agent calls three real tools in sequence — live data, no mocking, any model.

---

## Why This Exists

Most AI agent demos fall into one of two traps:
- **Too simple** — one provider, one tool, hardcoded in a 50-line script.
- **Too complex** — a sprawling framework that hides how anything actually works.

This project is a **fully working vertical slice**: MCP server → agent loop → LLM routing → Streamlit UI, with every layer visible and replaceable. It's designed to be the thing you read when you want to understand how MCP and the Responses API actually wire together — then fork and build something real from.

## Why Use It

| If you want to... | This gives you... |
|---|---|
| Understand MCP in practice | A real stdio server with 3 live tools, not a toy example |
| Switch LLM providers without rewriting | One model string change, everything else stays |
| Chain multiple tool calls automatically | The agent loop handles it — no manual orchestration |
| See the Responses API in action locally | The runtime runs the full spec at `localhost:8080` |
| Build on top of this | Clean 4-file architecture, every component independently replaceable |

---

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    UI["🖥 streamlit_app.py\nor run_demo.py"]
    Agent["🧠 agent_loop.py\nOrchestrates the agentic loop"]
    MCP["⚡ mcp_server.py\nMCP Tool Server (stdio subprocess)"]
    Client["🔌 openresponses_client.py\nOpenAI SDK → localhost:8080"]
    Runtime["🐳 OpenResponses Runtime\nHardened Julep fork on Docker"]
    LiteLLM["🔀 LiteLLM (inside Docker)\nRoutes to real providers"]
    Groq["Groq API"]
    Gemini["Gemini API"]
    Other["Other providers..."]
    Weather["🌤 Open-Meteo\nWeather API"]
    Geo["🗺 Open-Meteo\nGeocoding API"]
    Time["🕐 Python zoneinfo\nTimezone library"]

    UI --> Agent
    Agent --> MCP
    Agent --> Client
    MCP --> Weather
    MCP --> Geo
    MCP --> Time
    Client --> Runtime
    Runtime --> LiteLLM
    LiteLLM --> Groq
    LiteLLM --> Gemini
    LiteLLM --> Other
```

### How a single query flows

```
User: "Weather in Agra + coordinates + current time?"
  │
  ▼
agent_loop.py discovers 3 MCP tools, sends query to LLM
  │
  ├─ Turn 1 → LLM calls get_weather("Agra") → 27.3°C, Mainly clear
  ├─ Turn 2 → LLM calls geocode_city("Agra") → Lat 27.18, Lon 78.01
  ├─ Turn 3 → LLM calls get_current_time("Asia/Kolkata") → 12:29 PM IST
  └─ Turn 4 → LLM synthesizes all 3 results → final answer
```

---

## Providers (out of the box)

| Model | ID | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| Groq Llama 3.3 70B | `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | Production |
| Groq Llama 3.1 8B | `groq/llama-3.1-8b-instant` | Production |
| Groq GPT-OSS 120B | `groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b` | Production |
| Groq GPT-OSS 20B | `groq/openai/gpt-oss-20b` | Production |
| Groq Llama 4 Scout | `groq/meta-llama/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` | Preview |
| Groq Qwen3 32B | `groq/qwen/qwen3-32b` | Preview |
| Groq Kimi K2 | `groq/moonshotai/kimi-k2-instruct-0905` | Preview |
| Gemini 2.0 Flash | `gemini/gemini-2.0-flash` | — |

Add any provider in one line — no other code changes needed.

---

## Credits

The local routing layer is built on top of **[Julep AI's](https://github.com/julep-ai/julep)** open-source backend, with two custom patches applied:

- **Provider allowlist** — expanded to support Groq, Gemini, and other LiteLLM-compatible providers
- **Postgres 17 migration** — compatibility fix for the TimescaleDB memory store

All credit for the underlying runtime architecture goes to the Julep team. This project adds the MCP integration layer, the agentic loop, the multi-tool chaining, and the Streamlit UI on top.

---

## Prerequisites

- **Python 3.11+**
- **Docker Desktop** → [docs.docker.com/get-docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker)
- **Groq API key** (free) → [console.groq.com](https://console.groq.com)
- Optional: Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic keys for those providers

---

## Setup

### Step 1 — Clone

```bash
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/YOUR_REPO.git
cd YOUR_REPO
```

### Step 2 — Start the OpenResponses Runtime

This is the local Docker service that makes the Responses API work for all providers.

#### 2a. Install and verify Docker Desktop

```bash
docker --version
docker compose version
```

#### 2b. Configure API keys

```bash
cd OpenResponses-Hardened-Runtime
cp .env.example .env        # Mac/Linux
copy .env.example .env      # Windows
```

Open `.env` and fill in your keys:

```env
# Keep this as-is — it's a local auth token, not a cloud key
RESPONSES_[REDACTED-GENERIC_KV_SECRET]"

# Add your provider keys here:
GROQ_[REDACTED-GENERIC_KV_SECRET]"       # required for Groq models
GEMINI_[REDACTED-GENERIC_KV_SECRET]"        # optional
OPENAI_API_KEY=""                            # optional
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""                         # optional
```

> ⚠️ Never commit `.env` — it's in `.gitignore`. The `.env.example` in the repo has blank keys by design.

#### 2c. Build and start

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

First build: 2–5 minutes. Creates two containers:
- `open-responses-api-1` — Responses API endpoint on port 8080
- `open-responses-memory-store-1` — TimescaleDB session store

#### 2d. Verify it's working

**Mac/Linux:**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/responses \
  -H "Authorization: [REDACTED-BEARER_TOKEN]" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "groq/llama-3.1-8b-instant", "input": "Say hello"}'
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**
```powershell
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "http://localhost:8080/responses" `
  -Headers @{"Authorization"="[REDACTED-BEARER_TOKEN]"; "Content-Type"="application/json"} `
  -Body '{"model": "groq/llama-3.1-8b-instant", "input": "Say hello"}'
```

✅ Success: response JSON with `id` starting with `resp_`  
❌ Got 500: run `docker logs open-responses-api-1 --tail 20` — usually a missing API key in `.env`

#### 2e. Container lifecycle

```bash
docker compose stop          # pause (keeps containers)
docker compose start         # resume
docker compose up -d --no-build  # restart with updated .env
docker compose down          # full teardown
```

---

### Step 3 — Install Python dependencies

```bash
cd ../mcp_openresponses
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

**Windows only** — set UTF-8 mode to avoid encoding errors:
```powershell
$env:PYTHONUTF8=1
```

---

## Running

### Streamlit UI (recommended)

```bash
streamlit run mcp_openresponses/streamlit_app.py
```

Opens at `http://localhost:8501`. Pick models in the sidebar, type a question, hit **Run**. Watch each model call tools live.

### Terminal demo

```bash
python mcp_openresponses/run_demo.py
```

Runs 3 preset queries across all configured providers, prints side-by-side results.

### Programmatic use

```python
import asyncio
from mcp_openresponses.agent_loop import run_agent

async def main():
    result = await run_agent(
        model="groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile",
        query="What's the weather in Tokyo right now?",
    )
    print(result["final_answer"])
    for tc in result["tools_used"]:
        print(f"  Tool: {tc['name']}({tc['args']})")

asyncio.run(main())
```

---

## Extending

### Add a model — one line

```python
# In mcp_openresponses/run_demo.py or streamlit_app.py
PROVIDERS = {
    "My new model": "groq/meta-llama/llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct",
    # ...existing entries
}
```

### Add a tool — one function

```python
# In mcp_openresponses/mcp_server.py
@mcp.tool()
def search_news(query: str) -> str:
    """Search for recent news articles on a topic."""
    results = my_news_api(query)
    return json.dumps(results)
```

All connected models discover and call it automatically at runtime.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| `500 Internal Server Error` | `docker logs open-responses-api-1 --tail 30` — likely missing/invalid key in `.env`. Fix key, then `docker compose up -d --no-build`. |
| Gemini quota exceeded | Free tier RPM/RPD limit hit. Wait ~1 minute or switch to a Groq model. |
| `ZoneInfoNotFoundError` on Windows | `pip install tzdata` |
| `UnicodeEncodeError` on Windows | `$env:PYTHONUTF8=1` |
| MCP server not found | Run from the repo root, not from inside `mcp_openresponses/` |
| `.env` changes not applying | `docker compose up -d --no-build` recreates containers with the new env vars |

---

## Known Limitations

The patched Julep runtime implements most of the OpenAI Responses API spec, but does **not** yet support `function_call` / `function_call_output` items in the multi-turn `input` array. The agent loop works around this by rebuilding the full context as a text prompt each turn — same outcome, fully compatible.

---

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. Some good starting points:

- **New MCP tools** — add a function to `mcp_server.py` and all models pick it up automatically. Good candidates: web search, stock prices, unit conversion, Wikipedia lookup.
- **New providers** — if you have an API key for a LiteLLM-supported provider, add it to `.env` and one line to `PROVIDERS`. Test it and open a PR.
- **Runtime compatibility** — the patched Julep runtime doesn't yet support `function_call_output` multi-turn input items. If you find a way to enable it, that would make the agent loop significantly cleaner.
- **Bug reports** — open an issue with the model you were using, the query, and the error output from `docker logs open-responses-api-1`.

### To contribute

```bash
# Fork the repo on GitHub, then:
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/YOUR_FORK.git
cd YOUR_FORK
git checkout -b my-feature
# make your changes
git commit -m "Add: brief description"
git push origin my-feature
# open a Pull Request
```

Please keep PRs focused — one feature or fix per PR.
